body:
Is this a leftover from development? Specular light appears too strong in Forward+ compared to Mobile and Compatibility. Setting Specular Strength to `0.2` roughly matches Mobile/Compatibility, so I assume this multiplier is the issue:

```suggestion
				light_compute(indirect_normal, L_view, normalize(view), 0.0, sh_light, false, 1.5, f0, roughness, metallic, specular_strength, albedo, alpha, screen_uv, energy_compensation,
```

diff_hunk:
@@ -39,6 +39,9 @@
 			If [code]true[/code], bakes lightmaps to contain directional information as spherical harmonics. This results in more realistic lighting appearance, especially with normal mapped materials and for lights that have their direct light baked ([member Light3D.light_bake_mode] set to [constant Light3D.BAKE_STATIC] and with [member Light3D.editor_only] set to [code]false[/code]). The directional information is also used to provide rough reflections for static and dynamic objects. This has a small run-time performance cost as the shader has to perform more work to interpret the direction information from the lightmap. Directional lightmaps also take longer to bake and result in larger file sizes.
 			[b]Note:[/b] The property's name has no relationship with [DirectionalLight3D]. [member directional] works with all light types.
 		</member>
+		<member name="specular_intensity" type="float" setter="set_specular_intensity" getter="get_specular_intensity" default="1.0">
+			The specular strength of the lightmap.
body:
```suggestion
			The strength of the lightmap's approximated specular lobe. This helps make lightmapped scenes look closer to real-time lighting, which is particularly noticeable for lights that use the [constant Light3D.BAKE_STATIC] bake mode. Only effective if [member directional] is [code]true[/code].
			[b]Note:[/b] The lightmap is only able to represent one light direction per texel, which means that the specular direction may appear to be incorrect in certain cases. This can manifest as specular lobes appearing to warp around as the camera moves.
```
It may be more efficient to compute the matrix inverse on the CPU and pass it through the lightmap data
respectively also in `render_forward_clustered.cpp`, `render_forward_mobile.h`, `render_forward_mobile.cpp`, `scene_forward_clustered_inc.glsl` and `scene_forward_mobile_inc.glsl`
if you compute `float l1_len = length(l1)` first, you can `l1/l1_len`, and reuse it in `specular_intensity` calculation below, saving one square root (not sure if compiler is able to optimize this)

pretty sure view is already normalized
```suggestion
				light_compute(indirect_normal, L_view, view, 0.0, sh_light, false, 1.5, f0, roughness, metallic, specular_intensity, albedo, alpha, screen_uv, energy_compensation,
```
same here, I would compute `length(l1)` first
Was there a reason why this code was moved outside the deprecated section? If not, it should be restored to how it was.

```suggestion
			vec3 L_view = normalize(lightmap_direction * lightmap_normal_xform);
```

This is mathematically equivalent and much cheaper

This branch needs to be a spec constant. We don't want everyone to pay the cost of this feature if they don't use it. 

The intensity should only be used when the feature is enabled
This needs to default to 0.0f. Given the nature of this effect, it is going to break in a lot of cases. Further, it has a huge visual impact which may not be wanted, so it needs to be opt-in
Same for the other renderers. Use a spec constant for the branch, but continue passing in the intensity value in a UBO. The spec can just be set to true whenever the intensity is greater than 0.0

body:
Update default value to fix CI error:

```suggestion
		<member name="specular_intensity" type="float" setter="set_specular_intensity" getter="get_specular_intensity" default="0.0">
```
The semicolons at the end of the uniform buffers in this file have to be readded, otherwise Compatibility shaders are broken
The equation order changes haven't been applied to the Forward+/Mobile renderers

This needs to be per draw call, not per scene. You should store `lightmap_has_specular` per lightmap, then you can cache the value in `GeometryInstanceSurfaceDataCache` during `_fill_render_list`, which you can use to enable the spec constant in `_render_list_template`. Make sure you also account for it when the repeat count gets incremented in `RenderElementInfo`.

Ideally this should be added as a sort key, but Forward+ does not have space for more bits anymore...
I think this is redundant to store in element info? You should already have access to `GeometryInstanceSurfaceDataCache` in the render list loop.

Hopefully my final complaint. `uses_lightmap` is also used for lightmap captures, which do not have a lightmap specular path, so enabling the spec constant for them adds redundant code to the shader. You may also end up accidentally indexing out of bounds with this since the `gi_offset_cache` would be encoded differently.

To fix it I'd probably have a local variable for lightmap specular like `uses_lightmap` and use that to set this field in the surface.
